summary: An announcement from BBN of a planned release of IMPSYS 2600, a major new IMP program, for May 15, 1972. It would be tried on an experimental basis and the older IMPSYS 2514 reloaded if problems occurred. Sites were asked to help load a new tape and avoid scheduling production work during the switchover. It was replaced by RFC 343.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN announced a planned release of new software for ARPANET IMPs. Sites were asked to help load it and avoid scheduling network production during the switchover.

subtitle: A planned BBN software change for the ARPANET's IMPs.

tldr.problem: BBN planned a major IMP software release that could cause unforeseen problems during the network switchover.
tldr.mechanism: The notice schedules IMPSYS 2600 for May 15, 1972, asks sites to help load the new tape, and provides for reloading IMPSYS 2514 if problems develop.
tldr.outcome: RFC 331 is an operational notice about the planned change and was obsoleted by RFC 343.

facts.label: System to reload if problems developed

sections.title: Planned Software Release
sections.content:
BBN planned to release IMPSYS 2600 on May 15, 1972, between noon and 3 p.m. E.D.T. The memo describes the release as a major change to the IMP program and says it would be experimental.

If problems developed, BBN would reload the current system, IMPSYS 2514, and reschedule the cutover.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN planned to test a major IMP software release on May 15. If it caused problems, the old system would be restored and the cutover delayed.

sections.title: What Sites Were Asked to Do
sections.content:
BBN planned to mail a new IMPLOD 2600 tape to all sites. On May 15, BBN staff would contact each site in turn, ask personnel to load the tape, and provide further procedures. BBN preferred that someone familiar with IMP operations be present.

The memo advises sites not to schedule production over the Network during the switchover hours because unforeseen difficulties might arise.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site was expected to load the new tape when BBN called. Sites were asked to avoid production network work during the change.

sections.title: Expected Effects
sections.content:
The notice anticipated no first-order effects for hosts because leader formats and message types were not changing. It says the statistics package had been extensively modified and that the Network Measurement Center had been notified.

The Very Distant Host option would be included in the new release and was expected to be activated around June 1. The detailed changes were to be described in a forthcoming revision to BBN Report 1822.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts were not expected to need changes because message formats stayed the same. The statistics package changed, and the Very Distant Host option was expected to be activated later.
